Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams working on robotics, foundation models, and intelligent perception.

title: ROS 2 Firmware Engineer (Robotics & Embedded Systems)
description:

**Position Overview**

We are looking for a **ROS 2 Firmware Engineer** to develop real-time embedded firmware and low-latency communication systems for advanced robotic platforms.

You will work at the intersection of embedded software, robotics middleware, motor control interfaces, and real-time operating systems. Your primary focus will be developing firmware for joint actuators and sensor acquisition, implementing deterministic communication over industrial fieldbuses, and ensuring reliable communication between low-level hardware and the robot's onboard computing system.

This role requires strong hands-on expertise in embedded C/C++, microcontrollers, real-time communication protocols, and Linux-based robotic systems.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop embedded C/C++ firmware for STM32 and ARM Cortex microcontrollers used in robotic actuation and sensor acquisition.
* Implement and maintain firmware using micro-ROS, FreeRTOS, or bare-metal embedded architectures.
* Develop deterministic, high-speed motor communication interfaces using CAN-FD, CANopen, and EtherCAT.
* Optimize communication and control data exchange to support high-frequency robotic control loops operating above 500 Hz.
* Configure, maintain, and optimize PREEMPT\_RT real-time Linux kernels on onboard control computers to minimize latency and scheduling jitter.
* Develop and maintain low-level device drivers and hardware interfaces that connect actuators, sensors, and embedded computing systems.
* Integrate embedded firmware with ROS 2-based robotic software architectures.
* Implement hardware diagnostics, fault detection, and automated emergency-stop (E-stop) mechanisms to improve system safety and reliability.
* Develop power-management and hardware monitoring firmware for robotic subsystems.
* Troubleshoot communication failures, timing inconsistencies, and hardware-software integration issues across the robotic platform.
* Collaborate with robotics controls, hardware integration, and edge systems engineers to support reliable end-to-end system operation.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Embedded Systems, Robotics, or a related technical field.
* Approximately 3–5 years of relevant experience in embedded firmware development, robotics software, or real-time systems.
* Strong proficiency in embedded C/C++ programming, including bare-metal and FreeRTOS-based development.
* Hands-on experience with STM32, ARM Cortex microcontrollers, or comparable embedded hardware platforms.
* Practical experience with industrial communication protocols, particularly EtherCAT, CAN-FD, or CANopen.
* Familiarity with EtherCAT implementations such as SOEM or SOES is an advantage.
* Experience with micro-ROS and integration between embedded devices and ROS 2 systems.
* Understanding of Linux device drivers, real-time Linux, and PREEMPT\_RT kernel configuration.
* Knowledge of deterministic communication, control-loop timing, interrupt handling, and latency optimization.
* Experience integrating motor controllers, joint actuators, sensors, or other robotic hardware components.
* Familiarity with hardware diagnostics, fault handling, emergency-stop mechanisms, and embedded power management is a plus.
* Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex hardware-software integration issues.

**Why Join?**

* Work on advanced robotics platforms involving embedded systems, real-time firmware, and hardware integration.
* Develop low-level software that enables precise and reliable robotic motion.
* Solve challenging engineering problems involving deterministic communication, control-loop timing, and hardware reliability.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across robotics, embedded computing, and motion control.
* Contribute to the development of intelligent robotic systems designed for demanding real-world environments.

**Work Location & Arrangement**

On-site at the robotics R&D facility in New Delhi, India.
